items.title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
items.summary: A recent analysis examines how AI data centers are increasingly securing direct, dedicated primary power generation rather than relying on utilities. Focusing on Anthropic as a case study, the report estimates that about 87% of the company's contracted U.S. power will come from gas and 11% from coal by 2028. The findings highlight a heavy reliance on fossil fuels to meet skyrocketing energy demands in the near term.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights the massive fossil fuel infrastructure expansion being driven by AI data center electricity consumption.

items.title: A Beginner's Guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
items.summary: A new beginner's guide explains how to set up a private, local AI chatbot on a Windows PC using tools like Unsloth Desktop and open-weight models such as Qwen. By running quantized models that fit onto consumer graphics cards, users can bypass cloud provider usage limits and subscription costs. The guide emphasizes simple installation without requiring command-line tools or complex Python environments.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a practical roadmap for running powerful AI models locally on consumer hardware for privacy and cost savings.

items.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
items.summary: Worker755 is a browser game where the player acts as a subagent to a real AI manager like Claude, GPT, or Gemini. The AI manager issues tasks through a terminal with strict timers, reviews the work, and files performance reports. Players can bring their own API keys or use server resources to complete shifts in a simulated sandbox environment.
items.why_it_matters: It offers an interactive and experimental way to experience being managed by an AI orchestrator in a game setting.

items.title: EL4CTEO/fast-anything: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with
items.summary: Fast-anything is a tool designed to profile Python, Node, Ruby, and other applications to find slow functions, which are then ported to Rust using a coding agent. It automatically records real calls, verifies that the Rust port behaves identically to the original code, and safely swaps it in for performance gains. The process is fully reversible and includes automated edge-case testing.
items.why_it_matters: It streamlines the process of accelerating bottlenecks in existing applications with Rust without needing to rewrite the entire codebase.

items.title: Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers
items.summary: OpenRouter has investigated and off-boarded three inference providers after security researchers identified data policy violations. The company also removed 125 endpoints from its Zero Data Retention program as a precaution and notified affected customers. They are now implementing ongoing technical verification and stricter security requirements for all providers on their platform.
items.why_it_matters: This highlights the ongoing security and privacy challenges in the AI inference ecosystem, where data handling policies may not always be consistently enforced by third-party providers.

items.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
items.summary: This paper investigates how to properly mix residual streams in hyper-connection neural network architectures without causing streams to become either completely independent or indistinguishable. The authors propose a geometrical contraction method called cmHC that forces residual matrices to explore deeper into the mixing space while preventing over-mixing in shallow layers. Experiments show that this method improves scalability and reduces execution latency on Ascend NPUs.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a mathematically grounded way to stabilize and speed up the pretraining of very large neural networks.

items.title: erkamyaman/safe-anything: Find the holes before someone else does. A fast, 100% Rust vulnerability scanner: XSS, SQL injection, leaked secre
items.summary: Safe-anything is a vulnerability scanner written in Rust that identifies security issues like SQL injection, XSS, and leaked secrets in codebases. It also scans AI agent configurations, such as those for Claude Code or Cursor, to detect risky settings. The tool is designed to be used in CI/CD pipelines and provides specific lines and fixes for every finding.
items.why_it_matters: As AI agents gain more control over development environments, this tool provides a way to audit the security of both the code they write and the agent setups themselves.

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: The authors study how to prevent video world models from generating physics violations where objects penetrate obstacles. They introduce NoPeBench to test for this issue and discover that hidden states inside existing diffusion transformers can already predict when a collision will occur. Based on this, they build NoPeWorld, a lightweight prediction framework that intercepts and corrects unsafe actions.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a simple, plug-in method to make video world models behave more physically realistically without retraining the underlying models.

items.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
items.summary: The developers introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, a 35-billion-parameter language model using a mixture-of-experts design with 3 billion activated parameters. It supports thinking-mode generation and combines historical memory with bidirectional attention blocks. The model achieves strong performance on coding and agent benchmarks while maintaining high generation speeds.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates an efficient mixture-of-experts model architecture capable of fast generation speeds and strong performance on software engineering benchmarks.

items.title: w01fb0ss/PiBot: Open-source, local-first AI agent team for your desktop: multi-agent group chats, computer use, browser, MCP, routines and a
items.summary: PiBot is an open-source desktop application that allows users to run teams of AI agents locally on their computers. These agents can perform tasks like editing files, running commands, and browsing the web, with a security feature that requires user approval for risky actions. The software supports various operating systems and allows users to choose their own AI models while keeping data like files and chat history on their local machine.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a local-first environment for managing multiple AI agents that can interact with a user's computer while maintaining privacy and security controls.

items.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
items.summary: Google Research introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that improves how transformer models handle information across layers. By using learnable weights to dynamically select and route features from previous layers, DCA avoids the information dilution common in standard residual connections. This allows models to achieve similar performance levels up to three times faster with minimal parameter increases.
items.why_it_matters: This architectural improvement addresses a fundamental limitation in deep learning, potentially enabling more efficient training of very large models.

items.title: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
items.summary: RoboTrack is a new benchmark and training dataset designed to improve how robots track objects during manipulation tasks. It includes RoboTrack-Bench, which features 307 human-annotated videos of real-world robot interactions, and RoboTrack-15M, a large synthetic dataset generated through simulation. The researchers found that training on this synthetic data improves the performance of tracking models on real-world footage.
items.why_it_matters: Reliable point tracking is essential for robots to interact with objects in cluttered, real-world environments, and this work provides the data needed to improve those capabilities.

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.summary: DeepMind researchers used teams of Gemini 4 agents to optimize quantum algorithms for scientific simulations, such as fusion energy and drug design. The agents collaborated and debated to find more efficient quantum circuits, which were then mathematically verified using the Lean theorem prover. This process resulted in significant reductions in the computational resources required for these complex simulations.
items.why_it_matters: By combining AI agents with formal mathematical verification, this approach makes it possible to optimize complex algorithms for future quantum hardware.

items.title: Learning Video Foresight Reasoning from Unlabeled Videos via On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: Researchers introduced Future-OPSD, a training framework that helps vision-language models anticipate future events in videos without needing external human annotations or large language model supervision. The method uses a special scoring system to focus the model on decision-relevant future information while ignoring irrelevant background context. This approach improves base model performance on open-ended prediction and closed-ended planning tasks by up to 15.9 points.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a scalable way to train video-based AI models to anticipate future actions more effectively without relying on costly external data labels.
